data.name: NoticeNoMagnetometerDetail
data.value: This device has no magnetometer — the mode's reference instrument. Only the gyroscope estimate is left, and its factory scale error of 1–3% shows in the width of the interval.

data.name: NoticeSensorMethodsDisagreeDetail
data.value: The magnetometer and the gyroscope report different speeds. The magnetometer's value is shown; the disagreement is listed separately and means the result cannot be trusted yet.

data.name: NoticeMagneticDisturbanceDetail
data.value: The field phase fits a straight line noticeably worse than usual. Move speakers, power supplies and anything magnetised further away.

data.name: NoticePhoneNotFlatTitle
data.value: The phone is not lying flat

data.name: NoticePhoneNotFlatDetail
data.value: Lay the phone flat, screen up. This barely affects magnetometer accuracy, but it does interfere with the accelerometer checks.

data.name: NoticeGyroZeroDetail
data.value: Stop the platter for 2–3 seconds to measure the zero offset. Without it the gyroscope reports a shifted speed.

data.name: NoticeNoGyroscopeDetail
data.value: Instantaneous speed, wow and flutter, and spin-up time are unavailable. The speed itself is measured by the magnetometer and does not suffer.

data.name: NoticeNotEnoughRevolutionsDetail
data.value: Let the platter make at least a few revolutions. Within 60 seconds the method reaches better than 0.05% accuracy.

data.name: LoadCaveat
data.value: The phone weighs 150–250 g — on a budget belt drive that alone can slow the platter down. What is measured here is the speed with the phone on the platter, not while playing. Compare against the acoustic mode.
data.comment: Required by §3.6: shown with every sensor-mode result.

data.name: NoticeInputProcessedDetail
data.value: Noise suppression or AGC appears not to have switched off. They remove exactly the clicks the main algorithm is built on, and the result cannot be trusted.

data.name: NoticeClippingDetail
data.value: The signal is hitting full scale. Move the phone away from the speaker or turn the volume down.

data.name: NoticeTooQuietDetail
data.value: The microphone hears almost nothing. Move the phone closer or turn the volume up.

data.name: NoticeAudioMethodsDisagreeDetail
data.value: The click period and the pitch deviation report different speeds. Most often this just means the record was not cut to 440 Hz — the clicks are the more reliable of the two.

data.name: NoticeNoClicksDetail
data.value: On a clean record in a quiet room there is nothing to lock onto. Try the lead-in groove or a gap between tracks.

data.name: NoticeNoNominalDetail
data.value: The pitch deviation is measured but there is nothing to apply it to. Choose 33⅓ / 45 / 78 by hand, or wait for the clicks to settle the nominal.

data.name: NoticeRecordTuningTitle
data.value: The record's own tuning is unknown

data.name: PitchCaveat
data.value: A pitch deviation mixes the turntable's error with the tuning of the recording itself: the band may not have played at 440 Hz, and the mastering may have drifted. The reference acoustic method is the clicks.
data.comment: Required by §4.3: shown with any pitch-grid reading.

data.name: NoticeNoiseGateDetail
data.value: In the pauses the signal drops to digital zero — no microphone in a real room does that. Input processing did not switch off.

data.name: NoticeAgcDetail
data.value: The long-term level stays constant while the short-term dynamics are alive. Automatic gain control is distorting the envelope.

data.name: NoticeRawInputUnavailableDetail
data.value: The system did not hand over an unprocessed stream. Measuring is still possible, but check the input diagnostics.

data.name: NoticeInputClippingDetail
data.value: The signal is hitting full scale.

data.name: NoticeInputTooQuietDetail
data.value: The level is below the working range.

data.name: NoticeDcOffsetDetail
data.value: The signal has a noticeable zero offset — usually a sign of odd processing on the input.

data.name: NoticeSampleRateDetail
data.value: The system delivered neither 44100 nor 48000 Hz. This does not affect accuracy, but it does say the capture request was not honoured in full.
